אֶחָד a prophet, a certain prophet, προφή-
της τις. Dan. 8, 3 אַיִל אֶחָד a ram. 1 K.
19, 4. Also where אֶחָד precedes; e. g.
אֶחָד קָדוֹשׁ a holy one, a certain angel, τὶς
ἄγγελος, Dan. 8, 13. Sometimes also in
the earlier books, as Ex. 29, 3. 1 Sam.
1, 1; seq. gen. as אַחַד הַבֹּרוֹת one of the
cisterns, i. e. a cistern, Gen. 37, 20; comp.
5. one only of its kind, i. q. only, alone,
sole, Job 23, 13. Ez. 7, 5. Cant. 6, 9. Arab.
وَاحِد unique, incomparable, وَحِيد id.
A. Schultens ad Job l. c. et 9, 5.
6. Repeated, אֶחָד—אֶחָד, one—ano-
ther, unus—alter, Ex. 17, 12. 18, 3. Also
thrice, 1 Sam. 10, 3. 13, 17. 18. In like
manner distributively, Num. 13, 2 אִישׁ
אֶחָד אִישׁ אֶחָד one man to a tribe shall ye
send, i. e. a man for every tribe. 34, 18.
7. כְּאֶחָד as one, i. e. together, at once,
Ezra 2, 64 כָּל־הַקָּהָל כְּאֶחָד the whole con-
gregation together. 3, 9. 6, 20. Eccl. 11, 6
שְׁנֵיהֶם כְּאֶחָד both together, both alike.
Also together, in company, Is. 65, 25.—
In the same sense is used כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד
Judg. 20, 8. 1 Sam. 11, 7. Chald. כַּחֲדָא.
8. Fem. אַחַת ellipt. for פַּעַם אַחַת one
time, once, 2 K. 6, 10. Ps. 62, 12.
9. בְּאַחַת a) i. q. אַחַת no. 8. Num. 10,
4. b) at once, i. e. suddenly, Prov. 28, 18.
c) i.q. כְּאֶחָד together, altogether, Jer.10, 8.
10. לְאַחַד אֶחָד one after another, one by
one, Is. 27, 12; and so Ecc. 7, 27 אַחַת
לְאַחַת.
Note. In the difficult and vexed pas-
sage Is. 66, 17, the common signification
is to be retained: those who sanctify and
purify themselves in or for the [idol-]
groves אַחַר אֶחָד after one, i. e. following
and imitating the one priest who directed
the sacred ceremonies. Comp. Com-
ment. on Is. l. c.
PLUR. אֲחָדִים 1. the same, Gen. 11, 1.
Comp. Lat. uni, e.g. ‘unis moribus vivere’
Cic. pro Flacco 26. Terent. Eun. 2. 3. 75.
2. joined in one, united, Ez. 37, 17
וְהָיוּ לַאֲחָדִים and they (the two sticks)
shall become one.
Deriv. the verb אָחַד, also pr. n. אֵחוּד.
אָחוּ (Milêl) an Egyptian word signify-
ing marsh-grass, reeds, bulrushes, sedge,
every thing green which grows in wet
grounds, Gen. 41, 2. 18. Job 8, 11. The
word was adopted not only into the He-
brew, but also into the Greek idiom of
Alexandria, where it is written ἄχι, ἄχει,
see Sept. Gen. 41, 2. 18. Is. 19, 7; like-
wise in Ecclus. 40,16, the author of which
lived in Egypt. Jerome in his Comment.
on Is. l. c. says: “ quum ab eruditis
quærerem, quid hic sermo significaret,
audivi ab Ægyptiis hoc nomine lingua
eorum omne quod in palude virens nasci-
tur appellari.” The Coptic translator has
retained the same word, writing for the
Gr. ἄχει of the Sept. ⲡⲓ-ⲁϧⲓ. Comp.
the same in Num. 11, 5. Kindred are
ⲁⲕⲉ, ⲟⲕⲉ, bulrush, reed. See De
Rossii Etymol. Ægypt. p. 24. Jablonski
Opusc. ed. te Water T. I. p. 45. T. II. p.
160. Peyron Lex. p. 16.
אֵחוּד (for אִחוּד union, from אֶחָד) Ehud,
pr. n. of a son of Benjamin, 1 Chr. 8, 6;
called in the parallel passage Gen. 46,
אַחֲוָה f. declaration of one’s mind, Job
13, 17. It is a verbal of Hiph. from r.
חָוָה, used in Hebrew only in Piel, but in
Chaldee also in Hiph.
אַחֲוָה f. brotherhood, Zech. 11, 14.
Denom. from אָח q. v.
אֲחוֹחַ Ahoah pr. n. 1 Chr. 8, 4, for which
v. 7 אֲחִיָּה.—Patronymic אֲחֹחִי Ahohite,
אַחֲוָיָה Chald. a declaration, showing,
explanation, Dan. 5, 12. Strictly inf.
Aph. from חֲוָה.
אֲחוּמַי (brother of water, i. e. dwelling
near it) Ahumai, pr. n. m. 1 Chr. 4, 2.
אָחוֹר m. (r. אָחַר) 1. the hinder part,
back-side, rear. Arab. أُخُرٌ id. Hence
a) מֵאָחוֹר from behind, i. e. behind, in the
rear, opp. מִפָּנִים, 2 Sam. 19, 9. Arab.
مِنْ أُخُرٍ. b) לְאָחוֹר backward, back,
Ps. 114, 3. 5; with averted face, Jer. 7,
24. c) בְּאָחוֹר backward, back. Prov.
29, 11 a fool uttereth all his anger, וְחָכָם
בְּאָחוֹר יְשַׁבְּחֶנָּה but a wise man keepeth
it back, q. d. drives it backward, so that
it comes back to himself. d) אָחוֹר in acc.
as Adverb, Arab. أُخُرًا, behind, on the

line_status.note: Printed order: אֶחָד stands to the right of קָדוֹשׁ, so in RTL logical order אֶחָד comes first — matching the preceding "Also where אֶחָד precedes". Reading B reverses the two words. Points as in A: אֶחָד with segol/qamets, קָדוֹשׁ plene with holem-vav and shin dot.

The only difference is spacing in the reference: the print sets "Jer.10," tight with no visible space after the period (the line is crowded, as "i.q." also shows), so Reading A matches; the Hebrew כְּאֶחָד (kaf with dagesh and shewa, segol, qamets, no vav/yod) is identical in both and correct.

Rightmost Hebrew word (first in logical order) is לְאַחַד with patach under both aleph and chet (not segol), and אֶחָד stands to its left — matching MT Is 27:12 and Reading A; Reading B reverses the order and misreads the vowel as segol.
Second Hebrew word is printed אֶחָד: segol (three dots) under aleph and qamets (T-shaped) under chet, not patach–patach as in B.

The word is printed in small capitals (full-height P, small-cap LUR) — all capital letterforms, so PLUR. not Plur. Hebrew אֲחָדִים (ḥaṭeph pataḥ, qameṣ, ḥireq, plene yod, final mem) is identical in both readings and matches the print.
The line is very tightly set; "40,16" is printed with no space after the comma (contrast "41, 2" on the line above), so Reading B is correct.
Three letters א-ח-י are printed (no resh, no fourth letter), ruling out B; under the aleph is a single horizontal bar (patach), not the two dots of tsere in A. Chet carries hiriq. Printed: אַחִי.

Under the ḥet the print shows a composite ḥataf‑pataḥ (shewa dots plus a horizontal pataḥ stroke), not a plain shewa; Reading B's אַחֲוָה matches, Reading A's אַחְוָה does not. Rest of the line is identical in both.
The mark above the khāʾ is a comma-shaped damma (ـُ), not a sukūn circle; the word is أُخُرٌ (ʾukhur), as Reading A has. Reading B's sukūn is wrong. All else (Latin text, punctuation) is identical.
The mark printed above the khāʾ is a comma‑shaped ḍamma (ـُ), not a ring‑shaped sukūn (ـْ), so the word reads أُخُرًا (ukhuran) as in Reading A.
